name: Chalkboard
summary: Drawn live with pastel chalk on a slate-green school board: broken grainy strokes, loose hatching, eraser smears and doodles.
description: The whole world is a Halloween blackboard drawing. Every shape is outlined with broken, pressure-varying chalk strokes, filled with a faint rubbed tint plus loose parallel hatching, and riddled with grain holes where the dark board shows through. Pastel chalks (orange, lavender, mint, butter yellow, pink, light blue) sit on a dark slate-green board framed by a wooden frame with chalk sticks on the ledge; enemies are wiped away by an eraser instead of exploding.
avoidFor: games needing photographic depth or dramatic lighting

difficulty.why: The loose stroke forgives imprecision, but every figure needs several 'redrawn' variants (line boil) and the ground is expensive to compute.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = clamp(round(screenH/360*4)/4, 2, 3.5) px per world unit; ground chunks at up to 2.5 px per unit (groundResMax 2.5, 256-unit chunks).
technique.summary: All art is drawn with a chalk toolkit (stroke / hatch / rub) into offscreen sprites, then a 128x128 grain mask is punched out with destination-out and a board-coloured 'eraser halo' is put behind the sprite so it reads on the busy hatched ground.
technique.linework: Chalk strokes resampled every 1 unit with +-0.12 unit jitter, split into runs of 3-7 points each with its own width (x0.78-1.18) and alpha (x0.72-1.0); closed shapes overshoot 1-3 points; a second offset pass at 45% width and 40% alpha. Outline widths: hero body 0.95, pumpkin head 1.2, small enemy 0.95, brute 1.5, props 1.0-1.2, details 0.35-0.6 world units. Round caps and joins.
technique.shading: No gradients as light. Volume = a flat 'rub' fill (alpha 0.1-0.72) + loose parallel hatching (spacing 1.0-1.7 units, width 0.35-0.5, angle ~0.7-1.1 rad) + a darker-chalk hatch patch on the shadow side (e.g. deep orange on the pumpkin lower-left) + a yellow hatch highlight top-right.
technique.lighting: Matte. The only 'light' is a soft orange radial rub behind the hero's head (alpha 0.32 -> 0, radius 14 units) and a yellow rub behind lanterns, both painted destination-over so they sit behind the chalk. Eyes and mouths are solid butter-yellow chalk.
technique.texture: Chalk grain mask (10% deep pits, blotches at half and quarter resolution) knocked out of every sprite, plus board smudges (+-16 brightness), old eraser swipes (huge faint arcs, alpha 0.026) and dust near the ledge.

paletteRules: The board colour #25332d covers most of the screen; chalk never fills an area to full opacity except eyes, mouths and tiny details.
Every chalk colour is a pastel; no saturated primaries, no black, no pure white (#eeeee5 is the brightest).
Each biome is identified by one chalk colour: meadow = mint tufts, forest = lavender cross-hatch, field = orange/yellow rows, frost = light blue rubs.
Holes inside sprites (ghost eyes, mouths, pupils) are filled with the board colour, never with black.
Wood brown only appears on the frame and the eraser; it is never used on the board itself.

typography.role: HUD numbers, damage numbers, card titles, kill counter
typography.css: font: 700 34px/1 'Cabin Sketch', cursive; color: #eeeee5; letter-spacing: 2px; text-shadow: 0 0 4px #1c2823;

typography.role: Big titles (level up, game over, pause)
typography.css: font: 400 78px/1 'Fredericka the Great', cursive; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #f9e58c;
font: 400 15px/1.3 'Architects Daughter', cursive; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #f89c52; text-shadow: 0 0 4px #1c2823;

typography.role: Handwritten words scribbled on the ground (decals)

background.summary: An infinite blackboard: per-pixel compositing of pre-baked tileable chalk textures (512x512) over a smudged board colour, with regions defined by noise fields whose signed distance gives crisp white chalk border lines, plus baked decals (eraser swipes, doodles, words, pebbles).
layers: Board base #25332d + macro brightness H (fbm /520, +-11) + smudge texture (radial blots and long swipes, +-16)
Region dust tint: 5-8% of the region chalk colour, fading in 0.9 units away from borders
Region chalk texture: meadow tufts / forest lavender cross-hatch / field orange-yellow rows inside Worley plots / frost blue rubs + snow asterisks; density 0.32-1.0 from a /150 noise
Region border: a 1-unit white chalk line where the signed distance is < 0.5 units, alpha 0.8 x grain; field plots get yellow 0.84-unit borders
Path: 17-unit-wide dusty band (+6 brightness) of stippled white dots, dotted borders at 1.3 units from the edge, pebbles
Decals: old eraser swipes (arcs r 60-140, width 14-26, alpha 0.026), doodles (star, spiral, bat, moon, heart, tic-tac-toe...) at alpha 0.5-0.72, Rock Salt words at 0.62
Props (y-sorted sprites): trees, dead trees, graves, fences, scarecrow, pumpkins, signs
Screen: edge vignette rgba(6,12,9,.5), chalk dust above the ledge, wooden frame with chalk sticks and an eraser

characters.summary: Simple doodle figures built from a few closed polygons (spline-smoothed): each shape is filled with board colour, given a translucent rub, hatched, and outlined with a chalk stroke. 4 walk frames x 3 line-boil variants (different random seeds) baked per character; facing by mirroring.
rules: Hero ~16 units wide, ~31 tall: big pumpkin head (ellipse 7.9 x 6.7, 6 subtle lobes) on a small trapezoid cloak and stick legs; head is 45% of the height.
Every shape first gets fillBoard() so overlapping lines behind it are hidden – that is how depth works in chalk.
Faces are solid butter-yellow triangles/ellipses with a board-coloured pupil – the brightest spot on any character.
Each enemy type owns one chalk colour (small = lavender cap on a cream bulb, ghost = white + blue hem, brute = lavender/pink cross-hatch with an orange core).
A board-coloured halo (1 unit, 12 offsets, alpha 0.6-0.9) is baked behind every sprite so it separates from the hatched ground.
Line boil: switch between 3 differently-seeded drawings at 7 fps, even when idle.

effects.name: Spawn: drawn onto the board
effects.how: The sprite is revealed top-to-bottom (rows = height x outQuad(spawnT)) with a 1.6-unit bright chalk-tip dot wandering along the reveal edge.

effects.name: Death: eraser wipe
effects.how: A wooden/felt eraser sprite sweeps horizontally across the enemy, the sprite is cropped from the wipe side, and a stretched ghost copy (x1+0.9u, alpha 0.45) smears behind; a tinted chalk smear stays on the ground for 2.6 s.

effects.name: Hit: scribble + crumbs
effects.how: A tiny chalk scribble (burst, zigzag or spiral, 0.22 s) at the hit point plus 2 chalk crumbs (small grainy quads) that fall with gravity 160 in the enemy's colours.

effects.name: Projectile: chalk seed
effects.how: Cream seed with yellow hatching and a white outline; behind it 3 rows of short broken white dashes that thin and fade with distance (the trail).

effects.name: Pickup and level up
effects.how: Pickups pop a 5-point yellow chalk star; level-up draws a rotating double chalk ring (yellow r 11.5 + orange r 9.6 with 12 ticks) and 8 stars flying outward.

effects.name: Dust puffs
effects.how: Dash and kills release soft chalk-dust puffs: 7 radial white blobs (alpha 0.42) + 18 specks, tinted per chalk colour, growing with outQuad.

ui.summary: HUD is drawn as chalk on the board: wobbly white chalk outlines with uneven border-radius, fills made of diagonal hatching stripes, Cabin Sketch numbers, Architects Daughter labels, and an SVG noise mask that gives every HUD element the same grain holes as the canvas art. A chalk-drawn clock with a pumpkin at 12 sits top centre.

motion: Line boil: every sprite has 3 variants with different random seeds, chosen by floor(time*7 + seed*3) % 3 (7 fps redraw jitter).
Hero walk: 4 frames, leg swing sin(phase)*2.6 units, body bob -|cos(phase)|*1.0; idle: 2 frames with a 0.45-unit bob at 2.2 fps.
Small enemy: 4 frames with +-0.09 rad body tilt and 0.9-unit bob; ghost: 4 wave frames at 5 fps, floats 2.2 units up and bobs +-1.1 at 3.1 rad/s.
Damage numbers pop from 60% to 100% size in 0.08 s, are tilted +-0.125 rad, and fade over the last 0.22 s.
Gems flip between 2 drawings at 5 fps and bob +-0.7 units; lanterns swap 3 variants at 7 fps.
do: Draw everything with the same three tools: stroke (broken pressure line), hatch (loose parallel lines clipped to the shape), rub (flat translucent fill).
Fill every shape with the board colour first so lines behind it disappear.
Punch the grain mask out of every baked sprite, word and HUD element.
Bake a board-coloured halo behind sprites so they read against hatched ground.
Give each biome and each enemy type its own pastel chalk colour.
Keep line boil running (3 seeded variants at 7 fps) – the drawing should feel alive.
Make destruction chalk-native: eraser wipes, smears, dust and crumbs.
dont: Don't use smooth gradients as lighting, glows with 'lighter' blending, or drop shadows with hard edges.
Don't use black outlines or pure white – chalk is #eeeee5 at most.
Don't draw perfect geometric lines; everything is resampled and jittered.
Don't fill shapes at full opacity – the board must show through (rub alpha <= 0.72 except eyes).
Don't use saturated or dark colours; no reds, no deep blues.
Don't regenerate strokes every frame – bake variants once and swap them.
performance: Expensive at init, cheap per frame. All characters (4 frames x 3 boil variants x 2 facings), props, particles, doodles and icons are baked at init (~0.5 s; extra boil variants are built lazily during the first chunks). Ground chunks are built incrementally with a generator (yield every row) inside a 5 ms per-frame budget: a 65x65 field grid, then a per-pixel composite of 512x512 textures. Per frame is only drawImage of cached canvases plus the clock hands. Hot spots: the per-pixel ground loop (Worley noise in fields) and the getImageData halo step when baking.
